target_customer: Indonesian consumers and small remittance users, later businesses needing local disbursement and business banking
problem: Sending money abroad from Indonesia was slow and awkward; the CEO says a bank errand to send money to a relative took over two hours. Transfez built a remittance app and later business tools.
business_model: Remittance fees and FX margin, plus B2B payments and spend products under the Jack brand
product_category: Cross border remittance and business payments (fintech)

founders.name: Edo Windratno
founders.background_notes: YC page lists no education or employers.

founders.name: Bondan Herumurti
founders.background_notes: YC page says he has worked in tech since 2010, starting as a web developer.

competitors.name: Monit
competitors.what: Indonesian spend management and corporate card startup described as the Brex of Indonesia
competitors.funding_then: Round led by 1982 Ventures reported February 2022

technical_complexity.rationale: Payments need banking and licensing integrations and compliance controls, though built on partner infrastructure.

defensibility.rationale: A Bank Indonesia remittance license is held per the company site, which new entrants must also obtain.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No acquisition found; Transfez continues and launched Jack in 2023.

market_need_then: Indonesia has a large diaspora and SME base and the company claimed 30x transaction growth during the pandemic and a 105 million dollar total volume run rate in 2021 per e27.

branding.domain_note: Uses transfez.com; the business brand Jack uses itsjack.com.

identity.voice_and_tone: Trust and licensed banking infrastructure for Jack

rebrands.why: Launched as a standalone business finance brand for registered companies; the CEO says Jack and Transfez are separate brands under one corporate entity

brand_strength.rationale: Regional fintech press covered the seed and the Jack launch, but no evidence of a strong consumer brand.

pivots.from: Consumer remittance with a B2B remittance add on
pivots.to: Added Jack for business finance and local disbursement
pivots.why: Demand from corporates for remittance and limited access to corporate credit cards, per the CEO

outcome_analysis: Transfez raised an undisclosed seed from East Ventures and BEENEXT in May 2021, joined YC in winter 2022 and extended into business payments with the Jack brand in 2023. It holds a Bank Indonesia license per its site. No later priced round or exit was found, so scale and funding after seed are unknown.
notes: Seed amount was not disclosed in the sources. One profile lists a seed in 2022-09, unverified and conflicting with the May 2021 coverage. Founded year 2019 from a DailySocial based account; other profile says 2020. The seed came more than a month before the batch. Remittance rivals such as Wise were not found in a dated source, so only Monit is listed.
